proof.surface: real envoy-dispatch built at 9cabeaf6 and a real nats-server 2.10.29, holders registered through the role and session buckets (t590probe): a live holder that never answers (ses_unans) and one that answers (ses_ans)
proof.command: RH-3 routed to role:t590-ans; RH-4 and RH-5 routed to role:t590-unans, three comments on RH-4; then 30 comments on RH-3 one a second, each one's latency from the write to ses_ans's forward (lat.sh/latcalc.py); then ses_unans restarted as an answering holder and every held event's forward order read per issue
proof.observed: 0 of 30 comments more than 1 s late, median 0.032 s, max 0.061 s (round 20 at fd93819c: 24 of 30, median 2.845 s, max 4.962 s; main's build at 0be366cf8a in round 20: 3 of 30). RH-4's three comments waited with attempt_count 0 behind its role-route event; once the holder answered they reached it as events 7, 10, 11, 12 in order, and all 15 silent issues' held events arrived in id order with no repeat.
proof.negativeControl: The same rig on fd93819c (round 20) delayed 24 of 30. Adversarial runs at this head that fill the four batch slots: eight silent issues arriving 1.2 s apart while 40 comments were written gave 2 of 40 more than 1 s late (max 1.765 s); five silent issues 0.25 s apart gave 2 of 40 (max 2.414 s, the first seconds only, while all four batches waited at once; their retries then share one batch). Bounded by concurrentBatches = 4; recorded for the reviewer, not a failure.

proof.criterion: Per-issue order across overlapping batches under load and through a SIGKILL take-over
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch processes at 9cabeaf6 on one database and one NATS; 20 issues routed to a role whose holder answers and prints each forward's event id
proof.command: load.sh x4: 50 comments each on LD-1..LD-20, alternating between the two processes; kill -9 of the publisher-hold holder 4 s into the load; then each issue's forwards checked for order, completeness and repeats against the events table
proof.observed: The other process took the publisher hold 6.07 s after the SIGKILL (00:00:03.851 -> 00:00:09.921); every LD event published; every issue's forwards in id order; every role-routed event reached the holder (the 20 issue.created events were published before the route existed and carry no role destination); one event (252, LD-12) was forwarded twice - by the killed process at 00:00:03.907 before its record, and again by the new holder at 09.950 - in order, the at-least-once repeat the holder drops by its dedupe key. The multiprocess suite's order tests pass (TestEachSessionTakesEachEventOnceAndInOrderAcrossTwoProcesses, TestAPublisherKilledMidBatchAndRestartedPublishesTheIssuesCommentsInOrderWithin10Seconds).
proof.negativeControl: Writes sent to the killed process after the kill failed (130 of 200 comments written), and none of them appears as an event.
